..
As of 330 PM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Breezy and mostly sunny Fall-like week for most.
Breezy NNE winds continue through the middle of the week, with 
mainly dry conditions expected.

Visible satellite imagery shows sprawling low pressure several 
hundred miles offshore of the NC OBX. An expansive cloud deck 
extends W of the center, currently overspreading coastal 
locations of our forecast area. Breezy conditions continue 
across the area, but especially so at the coast. Overall, wind 
speeds today have been lower than originally expected and the 
Wind Advisory that was in effect for Virginia Beach and coastal 
Currituck County has been cancelled. Wind gusts of 20-30 mph and
30-40 mph are possible inland and at the coast, respectively, 
through tonight. Outside of the wind, the weather should be 
remarkably uneventful this week as high pressure keeps most of 
us sunny and temperatures around seasonable levels. Dry 
conditions are also expected to prevail with low and comfortable
humidity values. Should note there is a low (<20%) chance of a 
rogue shower along the immediate VA and NC coast Tuesday night 
into Wednesday morning as the low potentially retrogrades 
westward a bit, but this would be dependent on the exact 
position of the low. 

Regarding temperature specifics, highs Tuesday through Thursday 
should be a bit warmer than today, generally in the upper 60s to 
lower 70s. A push of cold advection cools Friday off a bit, but not 
excessively so. The current temperature forecast ranges from around 
60 F on the Eastern Shore to the low to mid 60s for mainland VA and 
NC. The dry and seasonable wx should continue into the upcoming 
weekend, with the leftovers of the nor'easter/coastal system well 
northeast of the area and across the extreme eastern Canadian 
Maritimes by this time. Overnight lows remain on the chilly side and 
should average in the 40s inland and 50s near the coast. It could 
dip into the upper 30s in the rural locations well inland, with the 
best chances for this Wednesday night and Friday night. Can't rule 
it out tonight as well, though most of the typically cooler 
statistical guidance remains above 40 F. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Water levels gradually rise this week. Coastal 
Flood Advisories are in effect today into Wednesday night 
across the lower Chesapeake Bay, lower James River, and the 
Atlantic coast.

Prolonged onshore flow will produce tidal anomalies of 1 to 2 feet 
above normal astronomical tides. Fortunately, the region is 
currently in an astronomical neap tide cycle, which will help 
mitigate peak water levels. Even so, widespread minor to locally 
moderate coastal flooding is expected during high tides through mid 
to late week. All Coastal Flood Watches have been converted to 
Coastal Flood Advisories, with areas along the southern James River, 
southern Chesapeake Bay, Virginia Beach, and eastern Currituck (in 
previous Coastal Flood Advisory) now in effect through Wednesday 
afternoon's high tide and areas on the southern and coastal MD/VA 
Eastern Shore in effect with Tuesday afternoon's high tide through 
Wednesday afternoon's high tide.

Tidal levels are expected to gradually increase through Wednesday, 
with higher levels possible each day. The tidal anomalies currently 
are not trending as high as previous forecasts, which will result in 
nuisance to marginal minor flood stage tonight and early Tuesday's 
high tides along areas in the previous Coastal Flood Advisory. With 
the lower anomalies and lower NNE wind gusts, guidance has trended 
toward more widespread minor tidal flooding, rather than widespread 
moderate to locally major tidal flooding. It is likely that the 
current Advisories will need extended in time to capture Thursday's 
high tides. In addition, Coastal Flood Advisories will likely be 
need for the mid-upper Chesapeake Bay by Wednesday into the later 
portion of the week. There is also at least a signal that Bishop's 
Head may approach moderate flood stage Wednesday night or Thursday. 
A localized Coastal Flood Warning may be needed later in this week 
for any localized moderate stage flooding, depending on trends.
